Shared predictive importance with fold-internal residualization (UMFI-LR)

Source: R/shared_importance.R
shared_importance.Rd

For every anchor feature, shared_importance() residualizes the other predictors on the anchor using ordinary least squares coefficients estimated on the training rows of each resampling fold, applies the same coefficients to the assessment rows, fits the learner to the full representation (anchor plus residualized others) and to the reduced representation (residualized others only), and compares their assessment-set performance. This is the linear-regression variant of ultra-marginal feature importance (UMFI-LR) of Janssen, Guan and Robeva (2023), evaluated out of sample with paired folds.

Usage

shared_importance(
  x,
  y,
  learner = "rand_forest",
  metric = NULL,
  task = c("auto", "regression", "classification"),
  v = 5,
  repeats = 1,
  resamples = NULL,
  features = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  direction = FALSE,
  on_error = c("warn", "error"),
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

x

A numeric matrix or a data frame whose columns are all numeric. Missing values are not allowed.

y

The response: a numeric vector for regression or a factor for classification (binary or multiclass; the first level is the event level for probability metrics). Character vectors are converted to factors.

learner

"rand_forest" (default), "linear", a parsnip model specification, or a sharedimp_learner(). Hyperparameters are fixed; no tuning is performed. See sharedimp_learner() for details.

metric

A built-in metric name or a yardstick metric function. The defaults are "mse" for regression and "mn_log_loss" for classification. See as_metric().

task

"auto" (default: numeric y is regression, factor y is classification), "regression", or "classification".

v, repeats

Number of folds and repeats for rsample::vfold_cv(), used when resamples is NULL. Classification folds are stratified by y.

resamples

Optional explicit resampling: an rsample rset built on data with nrow(x) rows, or an integer vector of length nrow(x) whose unique values label the assessment fold of each row. Overrides v and repeats.

features

Optional names or indices of the anchor features to evaluate. Default: all columns of x.

seed

Optional integer. When supplied, fold generation and any stochastic learner run under a local RNG state seeded with seed, and the caller's RNG state is restored afterwards.

direction

Logical. If TRUE, also report the direction diagnostic: the correlation, on each assessment fold, between the anchor's values and the difference between the full and reduced predictions (probability of the first level for binary classification; NA for multiclass). It is a descriptive summary only and must not be read as a causal or conditional effect.

on_error

"warn" (default) records a learner failure on a fold as NA, aggregates over the remaining folds and warns; "error" stops at the first failure.

verbose

Print progress messages?

Value

An object of class sharedimp_result (see sharedimp_result) with elements importance (tibble: feature, importance, sd, n_folds, and direction when requested), folds (per-fold paired metrics; see fold_results()), metric, task, learner, direction, and bookkeeping fields n, p, v, repeats, seed, levels, resampling, call.

Sign convention

Let s = +1 if the metric is to be maximized and s = -1 if it is to be minimized. For each fold, importance = s * (metric_full - metric_reduced), so a positive value always means that keeping the anchor predicts better than the residualized others alone. Negative values are reported as they are; they are never truncated to zero. The reported importance is the mean over folds; sd is the sample standard deviation of the fold values and is a descriptive quantity only, not a standard error.

What the numbers are not

The values are out-of-sample predictive gains for a particular learner, metric and resampling scheme. They are not causal effects, not regression coefficients and not conditional effects, and the package deliberately provides no confidence intervals or p-values. See docs/specification.md in the source repository for the complete specification, including how the computation differs from the reference UMFI-LR implementation.

References

Janssen, J., Guan, V. and Robeva, E. (2023). Ultra-marginal Feature Importance: Learning from Data with Causal Guarantees. AISTATS 2023, PMLR 206:10782-10814. https://proceedings.mlr.press/v206/janssen23a.html

Examples

set.seed(1)
n <- 150
x <- data.frame(x1 = rnorm(n), x2 = rnorm(n), x3 = rnorm(n))
x$x4 <- x$x1 + rnorm(n, sd = 0.1) # near duplicate of x1
y <- 2 * x$x1 + x$x2 + rnorm(n)

# Fast, deterministic linear learner with the MSE metric
res <- shared_importance(x, y, learner = "linear", v = 5, seed = 1)
res
#> <sharedimp_result>
#>   task:       regression
#>   learner:    linear
#>   metric:     mse (minimize); importance = -(full - reduced)
#>   resampling: 5-fold cross-validation (1 repeat)
#> 
#> # A tibble: 4 × 4
#>   feature importance     sd n_folds
#>   <chr>        <dbl>  <dbl>   <int>
#> 1 x1         3.18    0.809        5
#> 2 x2         0.920   0.383        5
#> 3 x3         0.00634 0.0250       5
#> 4 x4         3.13    0.865        5
fold_results(res)
#> # A tibble: 20 × 7
#>    feature id    id2   metric_full metric_reduced importance error
#>    <chr>   <chr> <chr>       <dbl>          <dbl>      <dbl> <chr>
#>  1 x1      Fold1 NA           1.02           4.31    3.29    NA   
#>  2 x1      Fold2 NA           1.85           4.00    2.15    NA   
#>  3 x1      Fold3 NA           1.25           3.92    2.67    NA   
#>  4 x1      Fold4 NA           1.37           4.89    3.52    NA   
#>  5 x1      Fold5 NA           1.18           5.44    4.26    NA   
#>  6 x2      Fold1 NA           1.02           2.22    1.20    NA   
#>  7 x2      Fold2 NA           1.85           2.53    0.688   NA   
#>  8 x2      Fold3 NA           1.25           1.61    0.364   NA   
#>  9 x2      Fold4 NA           1.37           2.46    1.09    NA   
#> 10 x2      Fold5 NA           1.18           2.45    1.26    NA   
#> 11 x3      Fold1 NA           1.02           1.03    0.00905 NA   
#> 12 x3      Fold2 NA           1.85           1.89    0.0398  NA   
#> 13 x3      Fold3 NA           1.25           1.24   -0.00375 NA   
#> 14 x3      Fold4 NA           1.37           1.34   -0.0282  NA   
#> 15 x3      Fold5 NA           1.18           1.20    0.0148  NA   
#> 16 x4      Fold1 NA           1.02           4.49    3.47    NA   
#> 17 x4      Fold2 NA           1.85           3.69    1.85    NA   
#> 18 x4      Fold3 NA           1.25           3.92    2.67    NA   
#> 19 x4      Fold4 NA           1.37           5.03    3.66    NA   
#> 20 x4      Fold5 NA           1.18           5.17    3.99    NA   

# Binary classification with log loss
yb <- factor(ifelse(y > median(y), "high", "low"))
shared_importance(x, yb, learner = "linear", metric = "accuracy", v = 5, seed = 1)
#> <sharedimp_result>
#>   task:       classification (2 classes)
#>   learner:    linear
#>   metric:     accuracy (maximize); importance = +(full - reduced)
#>   resampling: 5-fold cross-validation (1 repeat), stratified by y
#> 
#> # A tibble: 4 × 4
#>   feature importance     sd n_folds
#>   <chr>        <dbl>  <dbl>   <int>
#> 1 x1          0.253  0.110        5
#> 2 x2          0.0667 0.113        5
#> 3 x3         -0.0133 0.0298       5
#> 4 x4          0.253  0.0606       5

# \donttest{
# Default random forest learner (ranger, 500 trees)
shared_importance(x, y, v = 5, seed = 1)
#> <sharedimp_result>
#>   task:       regression
#>   learner:    rand_forest
#>   metric:     mse (minimize); importance = -(full - reduced)
